description.text:
Add reference frames.

'Add All' will add all frames based on the input's start and end range. This will skip missing frames on the input clip.

'Add Range' provides a dialog box to add specific frames.
Add a new user track in the current frame.

When enabled, allows you to quickly lay down user tracks. Use Ctrl/Cmd+Alt click to turn this on and insert a user track.

Create user tracks before tracking and solving to lock the camera to a particular part of the shot. You can assign known 3D survey points to user tracks before solving to match the camera to known geometry. Alternatively, add user tracks after a camera solve to extract specific 3D points in the shot.
Set whether stereo cameras are aligned. The solve will then align secondary cameras to the principal camera position.
Anamorphic squeeze term (anamorphic lenses only).
Aperture
Asymmetric distortion.

Extend the selected user tracks using automatic tracking.

You can add a user track at a specific 2D feature on a single frame and use 'Autotrack' to automatically define the track in the shot. You can use this after the solve to extract a specific 3D point with 'Update XYZ'.

For stills, if the cache has been cleared this will need to recalculate the feature data which can be slow.
Equivalent value for the parameter b on Nuke's Card node.
Equivalent value for the parameter c on Nuke's Card node.
Rotate
Translate

Set the type of camera solve. Use 'Rotation Only' for a nodal camera move. Use 'Free Camera' for a rotating and translating camera. Use 'Linear Motion' for a straight camera path. Use 'Planar Motion' for a flat camera path.
Equivalent value for the scale parameter on Nuke's Card node, needed to reproduce the horizontal scale.
Checking this will cause classic 3D system nodes to be created.

Bake out new nodes for the calculated camera and scene.

Create new camera and point cloud nodes based on the results of the solve. The available options are: Camera: Create a Camera linked to the calculated projection. Camera rig: Create a multi-view rig with a Camera per view. Camera set: Create a set of Cameras, one Camera per solved frame. Scene: Create a Scene with a Camera and PointCloud for the camera solve. Scene+: Create a Scene with a Camera, PointCloud, ScanlineRender, and LensDistortion (Undistort) node. Point cloud: Create a PointCloud for the camera solve. Distortion: Create a LensDistortion node preconfigured for distortion using the same settings as the CameraTracker. You can use this node to distort your CG or other elements before comping them back over the input footage. Undistortion: Create a LensDistortion node preconfigured for undistortion using the same settings as the CameraTracker. You can apply this node to your input footage to make it match CG elements rendered using the calculated camera. Cards: Create a group of cards. SphericalTransform: Create a SphericalTransform node with rotation configured to stabilise the 360 scene. SphericalTransform (Metadata only): Create a SphericalTransform node operating on metadata only with rotation configured to stabilise the 360 scene.

Set the threshold to detect features.                 A high value selects prominent points.                 A low value selects points that are distinct in a local region.                 Using a low threshold to spread tracks out can produce a more accurate solve.

description.text: Recalculate the 3D position for the selected user tracks. Use this to update the 3D position of tracks that have changed or created after the solve.

Enable this option to manually specify all of the values for the local matrix applied to this op, or to expression link the local matrix to another op's matrix. Enabling this option disables the individual knobs above.

Select how you want the user tracks to display.

'All' displays all of the user tracks in the Viewer.

'Keyed only' just shows the user tracks when they have a key in the current frame. Use this to work with the subset of user-tracks that have a key.

'Minimal' displays the user tracks as semi-transparent cross-hairs when they are not keyed. Use this to show all user-tracks and highlight the ones that have a key in the current frame.

'Off' switches off user tracks in the 2D viewer.

User track table.

Create user tracks before tracking and solving to lock the camera to a particular part of the shot. You can enable or disable user tracks using 'e' before tracking or solving. When solved you can review the 'error' for the calculated 3D XYZ position. If the error is high, try reviewing the 2D xy feature track and disable it in the solve if necessary.

You can assign 3D survey points to user tracks before solving to match the camera to known geometry. Mark survey points using 's', the XYZ position is then locked and used in the solve. To attach a user-track to known geometry, display the thumbnail strip in the 3D viewer so that you can select and deselect user tracks. First select a track, then select a vertex in the 3D viewer and use the right-click menu to assign the 3D position to the user track.

User tracks can be created by adding a new user track then manually setting a key on each frame. In sequences you can use a Tracker node to create tracks and then import these as user tracks using 'Import Tracker'. Alternatively you can add a user track on one frame then use 'Autotrack' to automatically create the track in CameraTracker.

User-tracks may be required to manually connect frames in stills before tracking and solving. Automatic tracking can fail if there is a large change in view, for example if the change in overlap between frames is greater than 25%. Try placing user tracks to connect as many frames as possible. 1-4 user tracks can be sufficient to assist automatic tracking. For user-track only solves, 8-16 user tracks are required per frame.

User tracks can be created after a camera solve to extract specific 3D XYZ positions in the shot. The user track must be defined in 3 or more frames with good parallax to get an accurate 3D point. You can manually create a new track, import an existing track or automatically create a track with 'Autotrack'. Then use 'Update XYZ' to calculate the 3D position from the solve.

description.text:
CameraTracker

Use the CameraTracker to track the motion in a shot and calculate a virtual camera that matches the original camera motion. You can then match-move 3D elements to the 2D footage. The analysis must be performed in NukeX and the result can then be used in Nuke.

To create a match-move camera, set the input 'Source' to 'Sequence' then use 'Track' to automatically track the motion in the 2D footage, use 'Solve' to calculate the virtual camera, and then 'Create' to export a Camera to use with a ScanlineRender node.

The CameraTracker can also be used to create a camera for reference stills taken on-set. Set the input 'Source' to 'stills' then select the frame range that is required, use 'Track' to match the frames together, 'Solve' to calculate the camera and 'Create' to export a Camera node. This can be used with a ModelBuilder node to create set geometry.
